hits.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v1 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
hits.text: When a baggage handler finds a damaged, leaking, or unattended checked bag in the baggage make-up area, the handler must escalate the incident to the Baggage Duty Supervisor within 30 minutes of discovery and must report it under AP-INC-002. All incidents must be documented in the incident log and reported to the appropriate supervisory personnel. If a baggage handler identifies an issue that cannot be resolved independently, they must escalate the matter to the Baggage Duty Supervisor for further action. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that all incidents are investigated and resolved in accordance with established procedures. Escalation ensures that potential risks are addressed and that the integrity of the baggage handling process is maintained.

hits.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v1 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
hits.text: The baggage handler is responsible for the safe and efficient movement of baggage between the check-in belts, baggage make-up area, and aircraft loading zones. The baggage duty supervisor oversees the operations of baggage handlers and ensures adherence to handling standards. The ramp lead is responsible for coordinating baggage operations with aircraft crews and ensuring that all baggage is loaded and secured in accordance with safety protocols. All staff must follow established procedures, report any issues as required, and maintain clear communication to ensure the smooth operation of the baggage handling process.

hits.document_title: AP-INC-002 v1 Operational Incident Response and Review
hits.text: All operational incidents must be reported by the affected staff member to their supervisor or the Airside Duty Manager. The Reporting Staff Member is responsible for providing a clear and accurate description of the incident, including time, location, and any immediate actions taken. The Airside Duty Manager ensures that the incident is logged and that appropriate personnel are notified. For baggage incidents, the Reporting Staff Member must refer to AP-BAG-001 section 4 for escalation procedures. For restricted items, the Reporting Staff Member must follow the procedures outlined in AP-SEC-003. The first response should prioritize the safety of personnel and the integrity of airport operations.

hits.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v1 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
hits.text: This policy establishes procedures for the handling of checked baggage throughout the airport's baggage handling system. It outlines the responsibilities of staff involved in the movement and management of baggage, ensuring compliance with safety, security, and operational standards. The policy applies to all baggage handlers, baggage duty supervisors, and ramp leads. It ensures that baggage is processed efficiently and that any incidents or irregularities are addressed in a timely and consistent manner. This policy supports the safe and secure transportation of baggage and aligns with the airport's broader operational and security objectives.

hits.document_title: AP-BAG-001 v1 Staff Baggage Handling and Escalation
hits.text: All baggage incidents must be recorded in the incident log, which is maintained by the Baggage Duty Supervisor. The log must include details such as the time of discovery, the nature of the incident, and the actions taken. The incident log is reviewed annually to assess the effectiveness of the baggage handling procedures and to identify any areas for improvement. The Baggage Duty Supervisor is responsible for ensuring that the log is accurate and up to date. Annual review of this policy ensures that it remains relevant and effective in supporting the safe and secure handling of baggage.
